diagnostic_evidence.quote: We emphasize that our growth~conditions~on the gradient and Hessian noises are weaker than those assumed in \cite{Na2022Statistical}, and by a sharper analysis, our assumption on $\chi_t$ is relaxed from $\chi>1$ to $\chi>0.5(\beta+1)$. We~show that all their results still hold, with proofs deferred to Appendix \ref{pf:sec3:subsec2} for completeness.

Therefore, we only have to note that our growth conditions in Assumptions \ref{ass:2} and \ref{ass:3} on gradients and Hessians do not affect the proof of normality (though they affect the proof of convergence),~since the term $\|\bx_t-\bx^\star\|$ in the growth conditions converges to $0$ almost surely.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem sec3:thm2 claims the CLT for all beta in (0.5,1] with chi > 1.5beta. Its proof defers entirely to the proof of Theorem 5.6 of Na2022Statistical, which per the paper's own account was established under chi > 1. Whenever beta < 2/3 the admissible range chi in (1.5*beta, 1) lies strictly outside that hypothesis set, and the appendix provides no verification that the transferred normality argument (in particular the treatment of the stepsize-randomness term I_{2,t}) remains valid there; the only relaxation it discusses is the moment-condition one. Thus the stated theorem is unsupported as written in the regime beta in (0.5, 2/3), chi in (1.5*beta, 1).

failure_location.quote: The proof of asymptotic normality is almost identical to the proof of Theorem 5.6 in \cite{Na2022Statistical}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write out the normality argument under chi > 1.5beta, verifying each step of the transferred proof of [Na2022, Thm 5.6] with the weaker stepsize condition (the paper's own estimates E||I_{2,i}||^2 <~ chi_i^2 from Appendix E suffice to control the stepsize-randomness term at the sqrt(varphi_t) scale); alternatively restate Theorem sec3:thm2 under the stronger condition chi > 1, explicitly excluding beta in (0.5, 2/3).
issues.overall_effect: The asymptotic normality guarantee \eqref{nequ:4}/\eqref{equ:lyap} is unproven for beta in (0.5, 2/3); consequently the confidence-interval/region coverage guarantees of Corollary sec4:cor1, which combine this CLT with the estimator's consistency, are unestablished in that regime. The covariance estimator's own consistency (Theorem sec4:thm1) is not affected.
issues.title: Asymptotic normality (Theorem sec3:thm2) not established under the stated relaxed stepsize condition
issues.why_classification: The repair requires carrying out a contained but nontrivial CLT argument (adapting Na2022's proof with sharper stepsize-randomness bounds), or weakening the advertised regime chi > 1.5beta to chi > 1, which excludes a stated parameter range; a comparable normality result survives either way, so this is more than minor but not a loss of the architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We point out that $\hat{\Xi}_t$ can also serve as a consistent~covariance estimator for conditioned SGD methods, which follow the update form \eqref{nequ:3} though~$B_t$~may~not approximate the objective Hessian $\nabla^2F_t$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that Xi_hat_t is a consistent covariance estimator for conditioned SGD methods (AdaGrad, RMSProp, quasi-Newton) because Theorem sec4:thm1 'does not require B_t to converge to the true Hessian'. What the paper establishes: under Assumptions ass:1--ass:4 with B_t defined as the average of stochastic Hessians (eq. nequ:5), the proof of Lemma sec4:lem1 derives E||B_t - B^*||^4 = O(beta_t^2 + chi_t^4/beta_t^4) -> 0, and the whole error analysis of Theorem sec4:thm1 (the terms I_{3,i} via delta^i containing {B_i^{-1}-(B^*)^{-1}}grad F_i and (C_i-C^*)(x_i-x^*), and the approximation error theta^k via ||B_k - B^*||) relies on this derived convergence and on the Hessian-averaging structure. For conditioned SGD, B_t is not an average of stochastic Hessians and need not converge to grad^2 F(x^*); the limiting covariance is a different Lyapunov solution driven by the limit of B_t. No part of the paper identifies that limit or proves consistency of Xi_hat_t for it. The difference: a consistency guarantee for conditioned SGD is claimed; nothing beyond the sketched-Newton setting (where B_t -> B^* is derived, not assumed) is established.

failure_location.quote: Notably, Theorem \ref{sec4:thm1} does~not~\mbox{require}~$B_t$~to~\mbox{converge}~to~the true Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\tx)$, making our analysis directly applicable to conditioned SGD methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either withdraw/reframe the claim as a conjecture, or prove the extension: assume B_t -> B_infty (not the Hessian), re-derive the iterate decomposition and dominant-term analysis with the limiting covariance replaced by the Lyapunov solution driven by B_infty, and establish the analogue of Theorem sec4:thm1; a limited weakening of the claim leaves the core results intact.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed generalization of the estimator's consistency guarantee to conditioned SGD methods (Section sec:4.3 bullet) is unsupported; readers would take Theorem sec4:thm1 as covering AdaGrad/RMSProp-type updates, which the formal content does not cover.
issues.title: Overclaim: analysis claimed directly applicable to conditioned SGD where B_t need not converge to the Hessian
issues.why_classification: The claim cannot be fixed by a local edit without withdrawing an advertised generalization; a complete repair requires a new (contained but nontrivial) analysis with a different limiting covariance, while the paper's core results survive untouched -- more than minor, no major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Lemma aux:lem5 the auxiliary sequence is defined by phi-tilde_{t-1} = phi_{t-1} + sum_{i=0}^{t-2} (prod_{j=i+1}^{t-1} prod_k |1-eta_j sigma_k|) varphi_i phi_i (no division by varphi_{t-1}), and the proof then asserts the equality sum_{i=0}^t (prod_{j>i} prod_k |1-eta_j sigma_k|) varphi_i phi_i = sum_{i=t-1}^t (prod_{j>i} ...) varphi_i phi-tilde_i. Matching the i = t-1 terms shows the equality holds only if varphi_{t-1} = 1; since varphi_t -> 0, the right-hand side is smaller than the left-hand side by the factor varphi_{t-1} < 1 on the added finite sum. The subsequent bound via (appen:A1:equ1a) therefore controls a strictly smaller quantity than the original series, so the lemma's stated bound is not established by this argument. (The lemma's statement itself is true: inserting the normalization sum(...)/varphi_{t-1} into the definition of phi-tilde_{t-1} makes the identity exact and the remaining chain verbatim, since phi-tilde_i = phi_i for i >= t so Lemma aux:lem1's hypotheses are unaffected; alternatively the finite initial segment can be bounded separately by o(phi_t).)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the definition of phi-tilde_{t-1} to phi_{t-1} + (1/varphi_{t-1}) * sum_{i<=t-2} (prod ...) varphi_i phi_i, so that the asserted decomposition is an identity and the remaining argument applies verbatim; or bound the finite initial segment sum_{i<=t-2} (prod_{j>i} ...) varphi_i phi_i separately by o(phi_t). Both are two-line local repairs preserving the lemma's statement and all downstream rates.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof of Lemma aux:lem5 fails; this lemma supplies the kernel bound used to solve the fourth-moment recursion in the proof of Lemma sec4:lem1 (rate \eqref{xtrate}) and hence, transitively, the moment estimates used for the consistency and rate of Xi_hat_t (Theorem sec4:thm1) and the coverage guarantee of Corollary sec4:cor1. All these results become unsupported until the lemma's proof is repaired; the statements themselves survive.
issues.title: Invalid identity in the proof of the contraction-kernel Lemma aux:lem5 (missing 1/varphi normalization)
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the definition of phi-tilde_{t-1} (or a separate o(phi_t) bound for the finite initial segment) makes the proof valid; the lemma's conclusion, its role in Lemma sec4:lem1, and every substantive downstream claim and rate are preserved with no new argument needed.
